hints: Focus on how bonding in Period 3 oxides changes across the period, from ionic on the left to covalent on the right.
Remember that $\text{MgO}$ and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ are giant ionic lattices, while $\text{SiO}_2$ is a giant covalent network.
Look for the oxide that exists as separate small molecules held together only by weak intermolecular forces.
walkthrough:
**Recall the structure trend in Period 3 oxides**

Think left to right across Period 3. Metallic character decreases, so oxides change from giant ionic to giant covalent to simple molecular.

Trend: $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$, $\text{MgO}$, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ (giant ionic) to $\text{SiO}_2$ (giant covalent) to $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$, $\text{SO}_2$ (simple molecular)

**Sort the four oxides given**

$\text{MgO}$ is a Group 2 metal oxide, so giant ionic lattice. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is also giant ionic, though with more covalent character. $\text{SiO}_2$ is a continuous network of $\text{Si-O}$ single bonds, so giant covalent like diamond.

**Spot the simple molecular oxide**

Phosphorus is a non-metal further right, so its oxide forms discrete $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ molecules. Weak van der Waals forces between molecules mean simple molecular structure with low melting point, unlike the other three giants.

options.A: $\text{MgO}$ has a giant ionic lattice of $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\text{O}^{2-}$ ions with strong electrostatic attraction. It has a very high melting point, so it is not simple molecular.
options.B: $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ has a giant ionic lattice, with some covalent character due to the high charge on $\text{Al}^{3+}$. It is still a giant structure with a very high melting point.
options.C: $\text{SiO}_2$ has a giant covalent (macromolecular) structure with each Si bonded tetrahedrally to four O atoms. Breaking strong covalent bonds needs huge energy, so this is a classic trap if you think all covalent means simple.
options.D: $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ exists as separate discrete molecules held together by weak van der Waals forces. This gives a simple molecular structure with a relatively low melting point, making it the only simple structure here.
